case_name: Shyamal Ghosh v State Of West Bengal
respondent:
State Of West Bengal
Supreme Court of India

11 July 2012
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.507 OF 2007WITH
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO . 1369 OF 2007
ANDCRIMINAL APPEAL NOS . 539-540 OF 2011
The Judgment was delivered by: Swatanter Kumar, J.
1.  Eight accused, namely, Panchanan Tarafdar @ Chotka, Uttam Das, Dipak Das @ Mou, Manoranjan Debnath @ Behari, Bishu Saha @ Chor Bishu, Satyajit Das @ Sadhu, Ganesh Das and Shyamal Ghosh, were charged with offences under Sections 302, 201, 379, 411 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, the 'IPC'). All these accused were found to be guilty of the offences with which they were charged by the Trial Court vide its judgment dated 13th September, 2005. After hearing them on the quantum of sentence, vide order dated 14th September, 2005, finding the offence to be that in the category of rarest of the rare cases, the Trial Court awarded sentence of death to all the accused persons for the offence u/s. 302 IPC and directed that they be hange
facts: Eight accused were charged with offences under Sections 302, 201, 379, 411 read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code.
All eight accused were found guilty by the Trial Court and sentenced to death for the offence u/s.302 IPC.
The High Court acquitted all the accused persons of the offence u/s.379 read with S.34 IPC but sustained their conviction u/s.302 read with S.34 IPC and awarded them rigorous imprisonment for life.

The case was challenged before this Court by accused Shyamal Ghosh, Manoranjan Debnath @ Behari, Panchanan Tarafdar @ Chotka, Uttam Das, Ganesh Das, Bishu Saha @ Chor Bishu, Satyajit Das @ Sadhu and Dipak Das @ Mou.
issues: Whether the conviction of the accused persons is ill-founded?
Whether the evidence against the accused is weak?
Whether the crucial witnesses of the prosecution are reliable?
petitioner_arguments: The crucial witnesses of the prosecution, particularly PW8, Binode Mallick, PW17, Amal Ray and PW19, Kali Das have not named accused Shyamal Ghosh.
These witnesses are not reliable and their statements could not form the basis of conviction of the accused persons.
PW9, Haru Das, has not named any of the accused and the disposal of the dead body which is a material circumstance has not been proved in accordance with law.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has established the complete chain of events so as to substantiate the conviction of the accused.
The evidence against the accused is strong and nothing has been recovered from the accused Shyamal Ghosh.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the crucial witnesses of the prosecution are reliable and their statements form the basis of conviction of the accused persons.
The Court found that the evidence against the accused is strong and establishes the complete chain of events so as to substantiate the conviction of the accused.
holding: The appeals were dismissed and the conviction of the accused persons was upheld.
